Convert geometries between encodings

Source: R/convert.R
geo_as_wkb.Rd

geo_as_wkb() gives well-known binary as a list of raw vectors, ISO and little-endian, NULL for a null geometry; sf::st_as_sfc(), geos::geos_read_wkb() and s2::s2_geog_from_wkb() each read it directly. geo_as_wkt() gives well-known text, with every coordinate written as the shortest text that reads back to the same double, so the round trip is exact. Both carry the CRS as the attribute crs, since bare WKB and WKT have no place for one (design section 6.3).

Usage

geo_as_wkb(x, lossy = c("error", "warn", "allow"))

geo_as_wkt(x, lossy = c("error", "warn", "allow"))

geo_as_native(x, layout = c("separated", "interleaved"), type = NULL)

Arguments

x

A geo_vctr.

lossy

What to do when the conversion would lose information: a non-planar edge type on geometries with edges, which WKB and WKT cannot carry. "error" (a zugeo_edges_error), "warn" (a zugeo_edges_warning) or "allow". The CRS is never lost: it rides as the crs attribute.

layout

"separated" (a struct of coordinate arrays, as GeoArrow advises) or "interleaved".

type

NULL to infer, or one of "point", "linestring", "polygon", "multipoint", "multilinestring" and "multipolygon"; needed when every geometry is null.

Value

geo_as_wkb(): a list of raw vectors; geo_as_wkt(): a character vector; geo_as_native(): a geo_vctr.

Details

geo_as_native() gives a geo_vctr in a GeoArrow native type. The type is the one the geometries share, a single type promoted to its multi type where both appear; mixed types and geometry collections need WKB or WKT.

See also

geo_vctr() for the reverse, geo_crs_text().

Examples

x <- geo_vctr(c("POINT (1 2)", "LINESTRING (0 0, 1 1)", NA))
geo_as_wkt(x)
#> [1] "POINT (1 2)"           "LINESTRING (0 0, 1 1)" NA                     
#> attr(,"crs")
#> <zugeo_crs: none>
lengths(geo_as_wkb(x))
#> [1] 21 41  0
